nodes.title: Terminal visual coordinates, link opening, editor styles and input fidelity
nodes.body:
# Scope

User requested five bug fixes: cursor follows its real content row during scrolling; a visually wrapped link opens the full target; editor/code viewer retains styles; shell history never intercepts TUI input; multiline input displays and executes in original line order. Preserve terminal byte order, shell execution semantics, transport protocol and unrelated Agent Communion work.

# Acceptance

1. A visible cursor is anchored to its actual content row and column. User viewport scrolling and terminal region scrolling move that anchor; hide it when its content leaves the viewport. Presentation transactions may suppress intermediate cursor walks but must not pin a cursor to viewport coordinates or repaint it over unrelated text. Test frozen/unfrozen cursor, partial-region scroll, focus, blink, screen switch and scroll back to bottom.
2. Soft-wrapped URL/path segments resolve to one complete target from every segment. Preserve hard line breaks as separate text, Unicode cell coordinates, OSC8 precedence and existing URL validation. Test one/multiple wraps, punctuation at the wrap boundary, scrolling and exact target passed to the opener.
3. FileEditor and diff/code viewer mount with Monaco styles, readable syntax and correct cursor geometry in actual desktop and remote artifacts. Verify lazy loading, theme changes, close/reopen and CSS load errors with rendered UI evidence.
4. While a foreground TUI owns input, ArrowUp/ArrowDown reach that program and shell-history overlay remains closed after idle and scrolling, even with a visible cursor. Restore shell history only on an authoritative return to shell. Verify raw and semantic-delta paths, including actual loaded wasm exports and parser mode synchronization.
5. Paste/type a distinct numbered multiline input longer than the viewport and compare original input, PTY bytes, native parser grid/history, semantic-delta mirror and rendered rows. Both execution and display preserve order. Cover successive chunks, partial scroll regions, scrollback, resize and active render backend. Unit tests must identify the failing layer rather than assume input bytes are reversed.

# Current evidence and gate

Screenshots supplied by user show the same PowerShell input in correct native-terminal order and reversed groups in Ridge. renderer.rs refresh_frozen_cursor_cell preserves a frozen descriptor's row/column and reads that viewport cell; suppressed cursor selection does not apply scroll_offset. Wrapped-link joining and TUI keyboard lease already exist in source; deployed behavior is unverified. Do not replace these mechanisms without tracing actual failures.

At inspection, active lock BUILD-1e37f0bd3702 belongs to CHG-066. User confirmed another session is still working on it. stc verify CHG-066 reports POLICY_E_UNAUTHORIZED_DIFF for src-tauri/Cargo.toml. This proposal must not be applied or locked until that round completes; do not retire its lock, widen its paths, absorb its edits or mark it complete on behalf of this task.

# Required checks

After lawful lock: run focused behavioral regressions, npm test, npm run lint, npm run typecheck, relevant Rust tests, and real rendered/runtime verification for all five requirements. Build/rebuild the actual consumed wasm/frontend assets through existing build tooling when affected, without publishing. Complete the SpecTree verify/complete gates before claiming the repair is finished.

# Baseline verification (2026-10-09)

No implementation source changed in this round. Focused linkSpans/tuiGate/ptyWriteQueue/remotePaneBindings run: 4 files, 60 tests passed. npm run lint and npm run typecheck each exited 0 with one existing RidgePane.svelte:70 state_referenced_locally warning. First npm test run failed on remotePaneBindings.test.ts:72 5000ms timeout; isolated rerun passed. Second full npm test run had 226 files and 2118 tests pass, but exited 1 due to an unhandled window-is-not-defined rejection from TerminalManager.fitPane (manager.ts:5297), invoked by a pending timer at manager.ts:5081 after test globals teardown. Full test gate therefore remains failed. stc apply CHG-068 preview succeeded; no authoritative specs written. stc complete CHG-068 rejected with COMPLETE_E_CHANGE: lock belongs to CHG-066. These baseline results do not verify any of the five requested runtime repairs.

# Executed WASM root-cause probe

Loaded packages/ridge-term/pkg/ridge_term.js with initSync using the actual ridge_term_bg.wasm in Node, without rebuilding or modifying implementation files. Constructed TerminalKernel(24,80,200). Raw feed of ESC[?25l ESC[?25h produced visible=true, isTuiKeyboardLease=true and shouldAllowShellHistory=false. A second kernel applied a hidden Cursor delta followed by a visible Cursor delta, generated by e2eEncodeCursorDeltaFrame(1/2,0,0). For the ten-byte Cursor frame, offset 6 is visible; changing it to 0 produced bytes [6,1,1,1,0,0,0,1,0,0]. After this hidden frame: visible=false, lease=false, history=false. After visible frame [6,2,1,1,0,0,1,1,0,0]: visible=true, lease=false, history=true. Thus the consumed delta mirror never acquires the durable lease even across explicit hidden/shown cursor frames, while raw parsing does. terminal.rs apply_delta Cursor writes modes directly, without latching Grid inline_tui_sticky; DeltaFrame carries final-state cursor/modes and does not carry the native parser durable lease. A native chunk hiding then showing the cursor can additionally collapse into a final visible state. Fix must cover producer, mirror and relevant remote snapshots; simply adding a longer UI idle timer cannot repair missing authoritative ownership state. This probe proves the kernel routing discrepancy; actual foreground-process gates and deployed UI remain to be verified.

A separate raw WASM probe fed LINE_01 through LINE_20 separated by CRLF into TerminalKernel(6,40,100). Live visible rows were LINE_15..LINE_20, scrollbackLen=14, cursor=(5,7). After scrollUp(100), visible rows were LINE_01..LINE_06 and scrollOffset=14. This rules out reversal for that raw parser/history fixture only; it does not prove PSReadLine repaint, native delta, pixel-copy or real UI ordering.
# Executed wrapped-link coordinate probe

Loaded the actual WASM package and LinkSpanIndex from its existing TypeScript source directly in Node. Feed https://example.com/long/path?value=123456789 into TerminalKernel(8,24,100): every ASCII segment resolves to the complete URL. Prefix the same input with Chinese text plus a space (中文 ): WASM row 0 is 中文 https://example.com, row 1 is /long/path?value=1234567, row 2 is 89; rowWrapped flags are true,true,false. The actual URL occupies terminal cells [5,24) on row 0, but LinkSpanIndex reports [3,22). hitTest(kernel,0,23) returns null despite that cell being inside the URL. hitTest(kernel,0,3) also incorrectly identifies the full URL while the pointer is on the second wide Chinese glyph. Continuation segments still carry the correct full target. Cause: pushRawSpan copies RegExp UTF-16 offsets directly into terminal cell columns. A plain single emoji prefix happens to match two UTF-16 units/two cells, but that coincidence is not a general coordinate conversion. Fix must map text offsets through actual kernel cell widths/grapheme clusters, keeping merged targets exact. ASCII wrapping passes this fixture only; opener/deployed UI still unverified.

# Viewer entry scope correction

Remote MainApp lazily opens src/remote/lib/FileViewer.svelte, which uses its own scoped code-row, gutter and textarea styles rather than Monaco. Added that real entry to codeTargets and a focused FileViewer test target. Desktop FileEditor/DiffEditorModal and Remote FileViewer must both be inspected after the lawful lock. No build/index.html currently exists; source CSS alone does not establish the reported runtime styling failure. Do not infer a Monaco-only fix or claim restored styles from source inspection.

# Current gate recheck

CHG-066 remains DRAFT with lock BUILD-a18a7c073520. stc verify CHG-066 now passes authorization/trace checks (testStatus NOT_RUN), so its previous Cargo.toml authorization error is resolved by its owner; that is not completion and does not authorize this task's paths. User confirmed the owner is another active session. Do not complete that round or displace its lock.
# Independent worktree and concrete candidate

Created C:/code/wind-terminal-fixes on branch fix/terminal-five-bugs from source HEAD 3c461f35. Installed independent dependencies with pnpm install --frozen-lockfile and copied the existing ignored WASM package as a test prerequisite; workspace package links resolve within the independent worktree. Original C:/code/wind and CHG-066 remain untouched. Its inherited committed CHG-052 lock fails authorization against hundreds of existing files; approval to archive only that inherited lock and create this change's fresh lock has been requested explicitly because repository rules prohibit bypassing unfinished locks. No source implementation patch has been applied pending that decision.

Candidate .spectree/proposals/CHG-068-candidates/wrapped-link-coordinates.patch adds rowTextOffsets to WASM and consumes its map only after wrapped-span merging, preserving string-coordinate overlap detection before converting hit regions to terminal cells. git apply --check --unidiff-zero passes. An in-memory transpiled LinkSpanIndex candidate, fed the actual WASM visible rows and an adapter mapping actual cellsAt widths to UTF-16 offsets, passed ASCII, Chinese and emoji prefix fixtures. Each full wrapped URL resolves exactly, the visual row-end is hittable, and the cell before the true URL start is inert. This validates the TypeScript candidate with the proposed map; the new Rust export has not been built or tested yet. Keep this distinction explicit. The candidate must gain real Rust/WASM and integration regressions after the lock is established.
